title: Calculate Factorial Using Recursion
description: Read an integer N (0 ≤ N ≤ 10) and print N factorial using a recursive function. By definition, 0! = 1.

learning_content.title: Recursion and base cases
learning_content.intro: Recursion solves a problem by calling the same function on a smaller input. A base case stops the calls and returns a direct answer.
points: Define factorial for an integer n.
Use n <= 1 as the base case and return 1.
For larger n, return n multiplied by factorial(n - 1).
Each recursive call reduces n by one.
Print the result returned by the function.
learning_content.note: There is one recursive call for each value down to the base case.

quiz.question: What prevents the factorial function from calling itself forever?

options.label: The base case
options.feedback: The base case returns a result without making another recursive call.

options.label: The input statement
options.feedback: Input reads N but does not stop recursive calls.

options.label: The print statement
options.feedback: Printing displays a value but does not define recursion termination.

options.label: The function name
options.feedback: A function name enables the call; it does not provide a stopping condition.

quiz.explanation: The base case, n <= 1, returns 1 and ends the recursive chain.
